text:
Brandon Hagel is back. Tampa activated him off injured reserve in time for Carolina, and the Lightning have missed a forward who has quietly been one of the most effective in the league.

His numbers don't lean on luck. He has 13 goals on 12.6 expected and 24 points in 20 games, and Tampa takes 65% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, 12.1 points better than without him. That on-ice edge is elite. If anything the points have been held down: the Lightning have scored 8.3 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him out there, and that usually swings back. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) shows why the chances are good ones: he gets shots off passes across the slot and from behind the net, which go in about 25% of the time. Evolving-Hockey had him 16th among forwards in wins above replacement last season. A sixth-round pick, 159th overall, now projecting 73 to 99 points.
